headline: High-risk default interaction: Continue can write workspace files and use MCP, while Prefect can act on workflow metadata with broad egress, creating leakage and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could influence its instructions. Prefect does not expose a direct parsing bridge, but the pair shares filesystem-based state via Continue’s concurrency model, making injection plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF Continue ingests content from a shared workspace file as instructions
IF Prefect writes workflow metadata into a file that Continue later reads
mitigations: Restrict Continue to read-only access on shared folders
Separate workflow metadata from code workspaces
Disable MCP servers that emit untrusted text
Add a manual review step before acting on file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; Prefect touches workflow metadata and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or metadata can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or outbound requests in default configurations.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem workspace
IF either agent sends file contents to its backend or API by default
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for code and orchestration metadata
Redact secrets before either agent reads shared files
Disable outbound access for one agent during sensitive tasks
Store credentials outside shared directories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Prefect is an orchestrator that may also mutate workflow state externally. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so overlapping writes to shared resources can conflict even though Prefect’s direct write surface is not explicit.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same workspace or artifact directory
IF Prefect-driven tasks and Continue edits occur concurrently
mitigations: Serialize edits to shared artifacts
Use per-agent directories
Turn on file locking in the orchestrator
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or facts from editor context, and Prefect can operationalize workflow metadata. If Prefect consumes Continue’s output without verification, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into automated workflow actions. The pair lacks any documented verification or provenance controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF Prefect treats Continue-generated text as authoritative workflow input
IF Continue’s output is copied into Prefect automation without review
mitigations: Require human approval before Prefect executes generated changes
Add schema validation to all Continue-produced artifacts
Keep generated text separate from executable workflow definitions
Log provenance for every handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch. Continue handles source code and editor buffers, while Prefect handles workflow metadata; absent a documented regulated-data flow, compliance risk is limited to configuration gaps rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared workspace files
IF an operator routes PHI or EU PII through either agent without policy review
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Document data-handling rules for both tools
Review retention settings before deployment
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
